examples.ko: 훈민정음이 만들어지기 전에는 한자를 빌려 우리말을 적었어요.
examples.en: Before Hunminjeongeum was created, people wrote our language by borrowing Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 아이 이름을 지으려고 예쁜 우리말을 찾아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for pretty Korean words to name my child.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구가 우리말을 정말 잘해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My foreign friend speaks Korean so well that I was surprised.

examples.ko: 이 영어 표현을 우리말로 어떻게 하면 좋을까요?
examples.en: How should we say this English expression in Korean?

examples.ko: 요즘 우리말에 영어 단어가 너무 많이 섞여 있어요.
examples.en: These days there are too many English words mixed into Korean.

examples.ko: 우리말의 높임 표현은 외국인에게 조금 어려워요.
examples.en: Honorific expressions in Korean are a little hard for foreigners.

explain: '한국어'와 같은 언어를 가리키지만 '우리말'은 한국 사람이 자기 말을 가깝게 부르는 느낌이 있어요. 외국어와 비교할 때나 순우리말(고유어)을 이야기할 때 자주 나와요. 외국인이 자기 입장에서 말할 때는 보통 '한국어'를 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the same language as '한국어', but '우리말' sounds closer, as Koreans talking about their own language. It often appears when comparing with foreign languages or talking about native Korean words. Foreigners speaking from their own side usually say '한국어'.

examples.en: Payday is the 25th of every month.

examples.ko: 월급날에는 친구들과 맛있는 걸 먹으러 가요.
examples.en: On payday I go out to eat something tasty with friends.
When payday comes, I pay my card bill first.

examples.ko: 이번 월급날에 부모님께 용돈을 드릴 거예요.
examples.en: On this payday I'm going to give my parents some pocket money.

examples.ko: 월급날만 기다리다가 한 달이 다 갔어요.
examples.en: I just waited for payday and the whole month passed.

examples.ko: 월급날 전에는 돈이 없어서 집에서 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: Before payday I have no money, so I eat at home.

explain: '급여일'이라는 말도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 '월급날'이 자연스러워요. '월급이 들어오다'처럼 돈이 통장에 들어오는 표현과 같이 자주 써요. '월급날이다!'처럼 기쁜 기분을 말할 때도 좋아요.
explain_en: There is also the word '급여일', but in daily talk '월급날' sounds natural. It goes well with phrases like '월급이 들어오다' (the pay comes into your account). You can also say '월급날이다!' to share a happy mood.

examples.ko: 학교 근처에 싼 월세방을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a cheap rented room near school.
At first I lived alone in a small rented room.

examples.ko: 월세방은 보증금이 적은 대신 매달 돈을 내야 해요.
examples.en: With a monthly-rent room, the deposit is small but you pay every month.
For a monthly-rent room, it's spacious and clean.
My goal is to move from a monthly-rent room to a jeonse house.

examples.ko: 지금 월세방에 살지만 곧 이사할 거예요.
examples.en: I live in a rented room now, but I'll move soon.

explain: '월세'는 매달 내는 집값이고 '전세'는 큰 보증금을 맡기고 사는 방식이라서 둘을 구분해서 말해요. '월세방'은 보통 작은 방이나 원룸처럼 혼자 사는 방을 떠올리게 해요. '월세방을 구하다', '월세방에 살다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '월세' is rent paid monthly, while '전세' means leaving a large deposit to live in a place, so Koreans distinguish the two. '월세방' usually brings to mind a small room or studio for one person. Say '월세방을 구하다' (look for) or '월세방에 살다' (live in).

examples.ko: 윗집에 아이들이 이사 와서 집이 시끄러워졌어요.
examples.en: Children moved into the apartment above, so my home got noisy.

examples.ko: 윗집 소음 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep because of the noise from upstairs.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 윗집에서 물이 새서 천장이 젖었어요.
examples.en: Last night water leaked from the apartment above and the ceiling got wet.
The person from upstairs came by and apologized in person.

examples.ko: 우리는 윗집과 사이가 좋아서 가끔 음식도 나눠 먹어요.
examples.en: We get along well with the people upstairs and sometimes share food.

examples.ko: 너무 시끄러워서 윗집에 올라가 조용히 해 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: It was so loud that I went up and asked them to be quiet.

explain: 반대말은 '아랫집'이고 아파트에서는 '위층', '아래층'이라고도 많이 말해요. 층간 소음 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. 어떤 집의 위에 있는 집을 가리키니까 '우리 윗집'처럼 기준이 되는 집이 있어야 해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '아랫집', and in apartments people also say '위층' and '아래층'. It comes up a lot when talking about noise between floors. It points to the home above a certain home, so it needs a reference, like '우리 윗집' (the home above ours).

examples.en: The shop's glass door says 'Please pull'.

examples.ko: 유리문을 밀고 들어가니 시원한 바람이 불었어요.
examples.en: When I pushed open the glass door, a cool breeze blew.
A bird hit the glass door and I was startled.

examples.ko: 유리문 너머로 아이들이 노는 모습이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see the children playing beyond the glass door.
Close the glass door carefully so it doesn't break.
The whole front of this shop is glass doors.

explain: '유리창'은 열어서 바깥을 보는 창이고 '유리문'은 열고 드나드는 문이에요. 가게 입구나 베란다 문을 말할 때 자주 써요. '유리문을 밀다/당기다/열다'처럼 같이 써요.
explain_en: '유리창' is a window you look out of, while '유리문' is a door you go in and out through. It's often used for shop entrances or balcony doors. It goes with verbs like '밀다' (push), '당기다' (pull), and '열다' (open).

examples.en: I poured cold water into a glass and drank it.
Guests came, so I took out the pretty glasses.
Wash the glass carefully so it doesn't break.

examples.ko: 선반 위에 있는 유리잔 좀 내려 주실래요?
examples.en: Could you take down the glass on the shelf?
This glass is one my grandmother used.

examples.ko: 유리잔 두 개에 주스를 가득 채웠어요.
examples.en: I filled two glasses to the top with juice.

explain: '유리컵'과 바꿔 쓰는 일이 많지만, '잔'이 들어가서 손님상에 내는 그릇 느낌이 조금 더 있어요. '물잔', '찻잔'처럼 '-잔'으로 끝나는 말이 많아요. '유리잔에 따르다', '유리잔을 깨다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is often used interchangeably with '유리컵', but the '잔' gives it a slightly more 'something you set out for guests' feel. Many words end in '-잔', like '물잔' and '찻잔'. Say '유리잔에 따르다' (pour into) or '유리잔을 깨다' (break).

examples.en: The glass cup broke. Be careful.
I put ice in the glass cup and poured juice.

examples.ko: 아이가 있어서 유리컵 대신 플라스틱 컵을 써요.
examples.en: We have a child, so we use plastic cups instead of glass ones.
I almost cut my hand while washing a glass cup.
I bought three new glass cups.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물을 부으면 유리컵이 깨질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pour hot water in, the glass cup can break.

explain: 종이컵, 플라스틱 컵, 머그컵과 구분해서 재료를 말할 때 써요. 컵은 '개'로 세요. 깨지기 쉬운 물건이라 '깨지다', '조심하다'와 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it to specify the material, as opposed to a paper cup, plastic cup, or mug. You count cups with '개'. Since it's fragile, it often appears with '깨지다' (to break) and '조심하다' (to be careful).

examples.en: I came in second in the race.
Our team unfortunately came in second.

examples.ko: 저는 마라톤에서 이등 한 친구를 응원했어요.
examples.en: I cheered for a friend who took second place in the marathon.

examples.ko: 동생이 반에서 이등을 해서 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling placed second in class and got a prize.
I heard the second prize is a bicycle.
Second place is fine. You did your best.

explain: '일등, 이등, 삼등'처럼 순위를 말할 때 써요. '2등'이라고 숫자로 써도 읽을 때는 '이 등'이에요. 순서 자체를 말할 때는 '두 번째', '둘째'라고 해요. 반대로 맨 앞은 '일등'이에요.
explain_en: Use it for rankings, as in '일등, 이등, 삼등' (first, second, third). Even when written '2등', it is read 'i deung'. For order itself, say '두 번째' or '둘째'. The top place is '일등'.

examples.ko: 잠자기 전에 아이에게 이야기책을 읽어 줘요.
examples.en: I read a storybook to my child before bed.
I borrowed a fun storybook from the library.
The pictures in the storybook are really pretty.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 할머니 댁에서 이야기책을 많이 봤어요.
examples.en: As a child, I read lots of storybooks at my grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 이야기책은 글씨가 크고 쉬워서 한국어 공부에 좋아요.
examples.en: Storybooks have big, easy text, so they're good for studying Korean.
I don't know where this storybook went.

explain: 아이용 책을 말할 때는 '동화책'도 많이 써요. '이야기책'은 옛날이야기나 소설처럼 이야기가 중심인 책을 넓게 가리켜요. '읽다'와 '읽어 주다'를 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: For children's books, people also say '동화책'. '이야기책' covers books centered on a story more broadly, like old tales or novels. It's good to learn it with both '읽다' (read) and '읽어 주다' (read to someone).

en: this way and that; here and there

examples.en: I got lost and wandered this way and that.
I've looked everywhere, but the key isn't here.
People were looking at me from all around.
The kids run around in every direction, so it's chaotic.

examples.ko: 이쪽저쪽 둘러보다가 마음에 드는 옷을 찾았어요.
examples.en: Looking around here and there, I found clothes I liked.
It's so tiring trying to read everyone's mood on both sides.

explain: '여기저기'와 비슷하지만 '이쪽저쪽'은 이쪽과 저쪽, 두 방향이나 편을 떠올리게 해요. 그래서 '이쪽저쪽 눈치를 보다'처럼 양쪽 사이에서 신경 쓰는 말에도 써요. 움직이는 모양을 말할 때는 '이리저리'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '여기저기', but '이쪽저쪽' makes you think of two sides or directions, this one and that one. That is why it also fits phrases like '이쪽저쪽 눈치를 보다' (to watch both sides carefully). For describing movement, '이리저리' is also common.

examples.en: My maternal grandparents' house is a two-story house with a yard.

examples.ko: 언젠가 바다가 보이는 이층집에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: Someday I want to live in a two-story house with an ocean view.

examples.ko: 이층집으로 이사한 뒤 계단 오르내리기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Since moving to a two-story house, going up and down the stairs is tiring.

examples.ko: 옆집이 이층집이라 햇빛이 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: The house next door is two stories, so not much sunlight comes in.
Children waved from the balcony of the two-story house.
That two-story house has a red roof.

explain: '이층집'은 건물 전체가 2층인 단독주택을 말해요. 아파트의 2층에 사는 경우에는 그냥 '이층'이라고 해요. 숫자로 '2층집'이라고 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: '이층집' means a detached house that is two stories tall. If you live on the second floor of an apartment building, you just say '이층'. It can also be written with a number, '2층집'.

examples.en: I'm going to a language school to learn Indonesian.
Indonesian uses the alphabet, so it's easy to read.

examples.ko: 친구가 인도네시아어로 인사하는 법을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend taught me how to greet in Indonesian.
I have a friend who works as an Indonesian interpreter.
For me, Korean is harder than Indonesian.

examples.ko: 이 책은 한국어와 인도네시아어로 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: This book is written in Korean and Indonesian.

explain: 나라 이름 뒤에 '-어'를 붙이면 그 나라 언어 이름이 돼요. 영어, 일본어처럼요. 방법을 나타내는 '로'를 붙여 '인도네시아어로 말하다'처럼 써요. '인도네시아 말'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: Adding '-어' after a country name gives the name of its language, as in 영어 and 일본어. Add '로' to show the means, as in '인도네시아어로 말하다' (speak in Indonesian). You can also say '인도네시아 말'.

examples.en: Seven or eight people were absent from our class.
I bought about seven or eight apples at the market.

examples.ko: 일고여덟 살쯤 된 아이가 길을 물어봤어요.
examples.en: A child about seven or eight years old asked me for directions.
It looks like seven or eight people have gathered.
I took a train that takes seven or eight hours.

examples.ko: 어제 친구들 일고여덟이 우리 집에 놀러 왔어요.
examples.en: Seven or eight friends came over to my place yesterday.

explain: '일곱이나 여덟'을 한 번에 말하는 숫자예요. '명, 개, 살, 시간' 앞에서 '일고여덟 명'처럼 써요. 한자어 수로는 '칠팔'이라고 하고 '칠팔 개월'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It packs 'seven or eight' into one number word. Put it before counters like '명, 개, 살, 시간', as in '일고여덟 명'. The Sino-Korean version is '칠팔', often used in phrases like '칠팔 개월'.

examples.ko: 대학교 입학금을 내야 해서 아르바이트를 해요.
examples.en: I have to pay the university admission fee, so I work part-time.
The admission fee and tuition are paid separately.
I called the academy to ask how much the admission fee is.

examples.ko: 어학당에 등록하면 입학금은 한 번만 내요.
examples.en: If you register at the language school, you pay the admission fee only once.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 입학금을 면제해 주는 행사가 있대요.
examples.en: I heard there's an event this month that waives the admission fee.

examples.ko: 등록금에 입학금까지 내고 나니 통장에 돈이 없어요.
examples.en: After paying tuition and the admission fee, my account is empty.

explain: 입학할 때 처음 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 학기마다 내는 돈은 '등록금', 학원에서 매달 내는 돈은 '수강료'라고 구분해요. '입학금을 내다/면제하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It's money paid once when you first enter a school. Money paid each semester is '등록금', and monthly fees at an academy are '수강료'. Use it as '입학금을 내다' (pay) or '면제하다' (waive).

examples.en: Freestyle is the easiest in swimming.

examples.ko: 저는 자유형으로 백 미터를 헤엄칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can swim a hundred meters freestyle.
After learning freestyle, I learned backstroke too.
I watched the freestyle final at the Olympics.
In freestyle, the timing of your breathing matters.

examples.ko: 오늘 수영 시간에 자유형 발차기를 연습했어요.
examples.en: In swim class today we practiced the freestyle kick.

explain: 수영 종목으로 '평영, 배영, 접영'과 같이 나와요. 어떤 방법으로 헤엄쳐도 되는 종목이라 '자유형'이지만 보통은 팔을 번갈아 돌리는 영법을 해요. '자유형 100미터'처럼 거리와 함께 말해요.
explain_en: It appears alongside '평영' (breaststroke), '배영' (backstroke), and '접영' (butterfly) as a swimming event. Any stroke is allowed, hence the name, but swimmers normally alternate their arms. People say it with the distance, such as '자유형 100미터'.

examples.en: The small room is where the kids study.
I put a desk and a bed in the small room.
When guests come, we have them sleep in the small room.
You can see the playground from the small room's window.

examples.ko: 안방 말고 작은방 불을 켜 주세요.
examples.en: Please turn on the light in the small room, not the main bedroom.
We have so much stuff that the small room became like a storeroom.

explain: '안방'과 짝으로 써서 집에서 안방이 아닌 다른 방을 가리켜요. 방이 여러 개인 집에서 '큰방, 작은방'처럼 나눠 부르기도 해요. 크기를 비교하는 '작은 방'과 달리 집 구조 속 방 이름으로 쓸 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It pairs with '안방' (the main bedroom) to point to another room in the house. In homes with several rooms, people sometimes name them '큰방' and '작은방'. Unlike '작은 방' as a plain size comparison, it is often used as the name of a room in the layout.

examples.en: My younger son entered university this year.
Our younger son is really good at cooking.
My older son lives in Seoul and my younger son in Busan.
I've been worried a lot lately because of my younger son.
I gave my younger son a little pocket money.
I have two kids, and my younger son is still in elementary school.

explain: 아들이 둘일 때 '큰아들'과 짝으로 써요. 셋 이상이면 '둘째 아들', '막내아들'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요. 부모가 남에게 자기 아들을 소개할 때 자주 쓰고, 직접 부를 때는 이름을 불러요.
explain_en: With two sons, it pairs with '큰아들' (older son). With three or more, people often say '둘째 아들' or '막내아들'. Parents often use it when telling others about their son, and they call him by name directly.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에는 잡생각이 많아서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The night before an exam, I have so many stray thoughts that I can't sleep.
After exercising, the stray thoughts disappear.

examples.ko: 공부할 때 잡생각 때문에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: When I study, I can't focus because of wandering thoughts.
I listen to music to get rid of distracting thoughts.

examples.ko: 쓸데없는 잡생각 좀 그만하고 일찍 자요.
examples.en: Stop the pointless thinking and go to bed early.
I got lost in random thoughts while walking and passed my stop.

explain: '잡생각이 들다/나다/많다'처럼 쓰고, 없앨 때는 '잡생각을 버리다'라고 해요. 일이나 공부에 집중하지 못하게 하는 쓸데없는 생각이라서 조금 부정적이에요. 비슷한 말로 '잡념'이 있는데 글에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: Say '잡생각이 들다/나다/많다', and '잡생각을 버리다' to get rid of them. It's a bit negative, since these are useless thoughts that stop you from focusing on work or study. A similar word is '잡념', which you see more in writing.

examples.en: The teacher scolded the students who were playing around.
Don't mess around during class.
My younger sibling keeps pranking me, so I got angry.
The kids play around happily in the park.
I thought my friend was joking, but it was real.
The cat is playing with a ball of yarn.

explain: '장난을 치다'를 줄인 말이고 '누구한테 장난치다'처럼 상대에게 짓궂게 구는 일에도, 물건을 가지고 노는 일에도 써요. '장난치지 마!'는 장난을 그만두라는 말이지만, 진지한 상황에서는 '장난하세요?'처럼 화난 말투가 될 수도 있어요. 놀이를 나타낼 때는 '놀다'가 더 넓은 말이에요.
explain_en: It's a short form of '장난을 치다' and is used both for teasing someone ('누구한테 장난치다') and for playing with objects. '장난치지 마!' tells someone to stop messing around, and in serious situations similar phrases can sound angry. For play in general, '놀다' is the broader word.

examples.en: This drama is really fun.
My grandmother told me old stories in an entertaining way.

examples.ko: 재미난 이야기가 있으면 저한테도 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you have an interesting story, tell me too.
The movie I saw yesterday was more fun than I expected.

examples.ko: 할머니 이야기는 들을수록 재미나서 시간 가는 줄 몰라요.
examples.en: Grandma's stories get more fun the more I listen, and I lose track of time.
If a book is fun, I read it even if I stay up all night.

explain: '재미있다'와 바꿔 쓸 수 있지만 조금 더 친근하고 이야기하는 느낌이 있어요. '재미난 이야기', '재미나게 놀다'처럼 많이 써요. 반대말은 '재미없다'이고, '재미나지 않다'보다는 '재미없다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It can replace '재미있다', but it sounds a bit friendlier, like storytelling. It's common in '재미난 이야기' (an interesting story) and '재미나게 놀다' (to play happily). The opposite is '재미없다', which sounds more natural than '재미나지 않다'.

examples.en: Mom is setting the dinner table in the kitchen.
All the side dishes on the dinner table are delicious.
I'll help you clear the dinner table.

examples.ko: 저녁상 앞에서 아이들이 숙제 얘기를 했어요.
examples.en: The kids talked about homework at the dinner table.
Dinner is all set, so come on over.
I'll keep tonight's dinner table simple.

explain: '저녁 식사'보다 집에서 차려 놓은 상이 눈에 보이는 느낌이에요. '저녁상을 차리다', '저녁상을 물리다(치우다)'처럼 짝으로 써요. 같은 방식으로 '아침상'도 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '저녁 식사', it feels like you can see the table laid out at home. It pairs with '저녁상을 차리다' (set the table) and '저녁상을 물리다' (clear it). In the same way there is '아침상' for breakfast.

examples.en: The restroom is that way.

examples.ko: 길이 막히니까 우리 저리로 돌아서 가요.
examples.en: The road is jammed, so let's go around that way.

examples.ko: 우리 아이가 갑자기 저리로 달려가 버렸어요.
examples.en: My child suddenly ran off that way.

examples.ko: 저리로 가 보세요. 거기가 더 시원해요.
examples.en: Try going that way. It's cooler over there.
I saw the ball roll that way.
Everyone is crowding over that way.

explain: '이리로, 그리로, 저리로'가 한 세트이고, '저리로'는 말하는 사람과 듣는 사람 둘 다에게서 먼 쪽이에요. '저쪽으로'와 비슷하고 말투가 더 구어적이에요. 줄여서 '저리'라고도 하는데 '저리 가!'는 가라고 쫓는 센 말투예요.
explain_en: '이리로, 그리로, 저리로' form a set, and '저리로' points to a place far from both speaker and listener. It's like '저쪽으로' but more colloquial. It can be shortened to '저리', and '저리 가!' is a harsh way of telling someone to go away.

examples.en: Lower-grade kids finish class early.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 아직 저학년이라 숙제가 적어요.
examples.en: My child is still in the lower grades, so there's little homework.

examples.ko: 저학년 때는 친구랑 노는 게 제일 중요해요.
examples.en: In the lower grades, playing with friends matters most.

examples.ko: 이 책은 초등학교 저학년이 읽기에 좋아요.
examples.en: This book is good for lower-grade elementary students to read.

examples.ko: 저는 저학년 동생들을 가르치는 봉사를 해요.
examples.en: I volunteer teaching younger lower-grade kids.

examples.ko: 저학년에게는 긴 설명보다 그림이 더 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For lower-grade students, pictures help more than long explanations.

explain: 반대말은 '고학년'이에요. 보통 초등학교에서 많이 쓰는 말이고, 학교에 따라 어느 학년까지인지는 조금 달라요. '저학년용', '저학년 때'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: The opposite is '고학년' (upper grades). It's mostly used for elementary school, and exactly which grades count varies a bit by school. It often takes endings like '저학년용' (for lower grades) or '저학년 때' (when in the lower grades).

examples.en: I meet my friend at the metro station.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 전철역과 가까워서 출근하기 편해요.
examples.en: My home is close to the metro station, so commuting is easy.
There are lots of good restaurants near the metro station.
Where is the nearest metro station?
It rained, so I took a taxi to the metro station.
The metro station has so many exits that I get confused.

explain: '지하철역'이라고도 하고, 약속 장소를 말할 때는 '○○역'이라고만 해도 돼요. '전철역 근처', '전철역 출구'처럼 길 찾기나 집 위치를 설명할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: People also say '지하철역', and when naming a meeting place, just '○○역' is enough. It comes up in giving directions or describing where a home is, such as '전철역 근처' (near the station) or '전철역 출구' (station exit).

examples.en: This drink has zero calories.

examples.ko: 사고가 제로가 되도록 모두 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Everyone has to be careful so that accidents drop to zero.
My confidence is zero before the test, so I'm worried.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 설탕이 제로인 음료도 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop also sells drinks with zero sugar.

examples.ko: 오늘 제 체력은 거의 제로에 가까워요.
examples.en: My energy today is close to zero.
One bottle of zero cola, please.

explain: 숫자 0을 읽을 때는 수학에서 '영', 전화번호에서 '공'이라고 하고 '제로'는 '아주 없다'는 느낌으로 말해요. '칼로리 제로', '자신감 제로', '제로 콜라'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 외래어라서 일상 대화에서 가볍고 재미있게 들려요.
explain_en: When reading the number 0, Koreans say '영' in math and '공' in phone numbers, while '제로' carries the feeling of 'absolutely none'. It's common in '칼로리 제로' (zero calories), '자신감 제로' (zero confidence), and '제로 콜라'. As a loanword it sounds light and playful in daily talk.

examples.en: I'm a senior in college this year.
Now that I'm a senior, I worry a lot about finding a job.

examples.ko: 졸업반 선배들이 후배들에게 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: The graduating seniors bought a meal for the juniors.

examples.ko: 졸업반 때 친구들과 여행을 많이 갔어요.
examples.en: In my final year I traveled a lot with friends.
Our graduating class has thirty students in total.

examples.ko: 졸업반이라서 요즘 졸업 작품 준비로 바빠요.
examples.en: I'm a senior, so I'm busy preparing my graduation project.

explain: 졸업을 앞둔 마지막 학년이나 그 학생들을 말해요. 대학교에서는 '4학년'과 비슷하게 쓰기도 해요. '졸업반이 되다', '졸업반 학생'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the final year before graduation or the students in it. In university it can be used much like '4학년' (fourth-year). Say '졸업반이 되다' (become a senior) or '졸업반 학생' (a senior student).

examples.en: The children floated paper boats in the stream.
Please show me how to fold a paper boat.

examples.ko: 물 위에 종이배가 둥둥 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A paper boat is floating on the water.
A paper boat sinks quickly once it gets wet.
I put a small doll on the paper boat.
My child likes playing with paper boats.

explain: '종이배를 접다', '종이배를 띄우다'처럼 짝이 되는 말과 같이 외우면 좋아요. 종이로 접어 만드는 놀이라서 '색종이', '종이비행기'와 같이 나와요. 어린 시절 이야기에서 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: It helps to learn it with its partner verbs, as in '종이배를 접다' (fold) and '종이배를 띄우다' (float). Since it's folded from paper, it appears alongside '색종이' (colored paper) and '종이비행기' (paper plane). It often shows up in childhood stories.

examples.en: We decided to go to Jeju Island for this weekend trip.
I took a weekend trip to the nearby sea with friends.
I'm packing my bags to get ready for the weekend trip.
If the weather is nice, shall we go to the mountains for a weekend trip?
Last weekend's trip was so enjoyable.
I'll show you the photos I took on the weekend trip.

explain: 주말에 다녀오는 짧은 여행이에요. '주말여행을 가다/다녀오다'처럼 써요. 하루만 다녀오면 '당일치기', 하룻밤 자면 '1박 2일'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It's a short trip taken over the weekend. Say '주말여행을 가다' or '다녀오다'. A one-day trip is '당일치기', and one with an overnight stay is '1박 2일'.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 주소록에 새 친구 번호를 저장했어요.
examples.en: I saved my new friend's number in my phone's address book.

examples.ko: 주소록을 정리하다가 옛 친구 이름을 찾았어요.
examples.en: While organizing my contacts, I found an old friend's name.

examples.ko: 회사 주소록에서 이름만 검색하면 번호가 나와요.
examples.en: If you search just a name in the company directory, the number appears.
The address book is so long that it's hard to find anyone.

examples.ko: 주소록에 없는 번호라서 전화를 안 받았어요.
examples.en: It was a number not in my contacts, so I didn't answer.
I sent the email address book file to my friend.

explain: 휴대폰에서는 '연락처'라고도 많이 불러요. '주소록에 저장하다', '주소록에서 찾다'처럼 쓰고, 회사에서는 직원 번호를 모아 둔 '사내 주소록'도 있어요.
explain_en: On phones it's also often called '연락처'. Say '주소록에 저장하다' (save in) or '주소록에서 찾다' (look up in). At companies there is also a '사내 주소록', a staff directory.

examples.en: There is a big persimmon tree in the landlord's yard.
My rent was late, so I called the landlord.
The landlady brought me some kimchi.
I heard the landlord's family is moving this month.

examples.ko: 주인집 아저씨가 고장 난 자물쇠를 고쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: The landlord fixed my broken lock.

examples.ko: 저희는 주인집 아래층에 세 들어 살아요.
examples.en: We rent the floor below the landlord's.

explain: '집주인'은 집을 가진 사람이고 '주인집'은 그 주인이 사는 집이나 그 가족을 가리키는 느낌이에요. 세 들어 사는 사람이 이야기할 때 자주 써요. 옛날 이야기에서는 일하러 간 집, 즉 주인이 사는 집을 뜻하기도 해요.
explain_en: '집주인' is the person who owns the house, while '주인집' feels like the owner's home or the owner's family. Tenants often use it when talking. In old stories it can mean the house where one works, where the master lives.

examples.ko: 이력서에 붙일 증명사진을 찍으러 사진관에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a photo studio to get an ID photo for my résumé.

examples.ko: 증명사진이 마음에 안 들어서 다시 찍었어요.
examples.en: I didn't like my ID photo, so I had it taken again.
ID photos for passports have a set size.
There are two ID photos in my wallet.
Do you need just one more ID photo?

examples.ko: 사진관에서 증명사진을 찍는 데 만 원 들었어요.
examples.en: It cost ten thousand won to get an ID photo at the studio.

explain: 여권, 이력서, 신분증 같은 서류에 쓰는 얼굴 사진이에요. '증명사진을 찍다', '증명사진을 붙이다'처럼 써요. 그냥 '사진'이라고 하면 일상 사진도 되니까 서류용일 때 '증명사진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It's a face photo for documents such as passports, résumés, and ID cards. Say '증명사진을 찍다' (take) and '증명사진을 붙이다' (attach). Plain '사진' can be any photo, so use '증명사진' when you mean one for documents.

en: pass through and come; come through; pass by on the way here

examples.en: I ran into my teacher as I was passing by the school on my way here.

examples.ko: 어려운 시간을 지나온 만큼 이제는 행복해요.
examples.en: Having come through hard times, I'm happy now.
On the way here, I passed a big market.
After coming through the tunnel, the rain suddenly stopped.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 오다가 지나왔는데 문을 닫았더라고요.
examples.en: I passed that shop on my way, and it was closed.

examples.ko: 힘든 시기를 지나와서 이제는 웃을 수 있어요.
examples.en: I've come through a hard period and can smile now.

explain: '지나가다'는 지나서 멀어지는 방향이고, '지나오다'는 어떤 곳을 지나서 지금 있는 쪽으로 오는 방향이에요. '지나온 길', '지나온 세월'처럼 지난 시간을 되돌아볼 때도 써요. 활용은 '지나와요, 지나왔어요, 지나온'이에요.
explain_en: '지나가다' moves past and away, while '지나오다' passes something and comes toward where you are now. It's also used to look back on time, as in '지나온 길' (the road traveled) and '지나온 세월' (the years gone by). Forms: '지나와요, 지나왔어요, 지나온'.

examples.en: The cost of books is separate from tuition.

examples.ko: 이번 학기 책값이 십만 원이나 나왔어요.
examples.en: The books for this semester came to a hundred thousand won.
I borrow books from the library to save on book costs.

examples.ko: 책값 때문에 사고 싶은 책을 못 샀어요.
examples.en: I couldn't buy the book I wanted because of the price.
My older sister paid for the books for me.

examples.ko: 등록금에 책값까지 합치면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Tuition plus book costs adds up to a lot of money.

explain: '책값이 오르다/내리다', '책값을 내다'처럼 써요. '밥값', '차비'처럼 어떤 것을 사는 데 드는 돈을 나타내는 '-값' 표현 중 하나예요. 한 단어로 붙여 쓰는 점도 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Say '책값이 오르다/내리다' (rise/fall) and '책값을 내다' (pay). It's one of the '-값' expressions for the money spent buying something, like '밥값'. Note that it is written as one word.

examples.ko: 책상 좌우에 작은 책꽂이를 하나씩 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put a small bookshelf on each side of the desk.
I arranged the books I've read on the shelf by date.

examples.ko: 책꽂이가 꽉 차서 새 책장을 사야 해요.
examples.en: The bookshelf is full, so I need to buy a new bookcase.
Dust flew up as I pulled a book off the shelf.

examples.ko: 책꽂이 맨 위 칸에는 사전을 꽂아 두었어요.
examples.en: I keep the dictionaries on the top shelf of the bookshelf.

examples.ko: 이 책꽂이는 벽에 걸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This bookshelf can be hung on the wall.

explain: '책장'은 보통 방에 놓는 큰 가구이고 '책꽂이'는 책상 위나 벽에 두는 작은 것을 말할 때가 많아요. 두 말을 바꿔 쓰기도 해요. '책을 꽂다', '책을 빼다'와 같이 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: '책장' is usually a large piece of furniture in a room, while '책꽂이' often means a smaller one on a desk or wall. The two are sometimes used interchangeably. It helps to remember it with '책을 꽂다' (slot a book in) and '책을 빼다' (pull one out).

examples.en: I woke up at night because of the thunder.
The thunder was so loud that the child cried.
The sudden thunder startled me and I screamed.
Our puppy is afraid of the sound of thunder.
The sound of thunder is heard later than the lightning.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 천둥소리와 빗소리가 섞여 들려요.
examples.en: When it rains, thunder and rain sounds blend together.

explain: 소리를 말할 때는 '천둥소리가 나다/들리다', 현상을 말할 때는 '천둥이 치다'라고 해요. 번개는 '번개가 치다'로 같이 '치다'를 써요. 소리를 흉내 낸 말로는 '우르릉 쾅쾅'이 있어요.
explain_en: For the sound, say '천둥소리가 나다/들리다'; for the event, '천둥이 치다'. Lightning also uses '치다', as in '번개가 치다'. A word imitating the sound is '우르릉 쾅쾅'.

examples.en: Every morning the garbage truck passes through our neighborhood.
The garbage truck's noise startled me awake.
They loaded the collected trash onto the garbage truck.
The garbage truck usually comes early in the morning.

examples.ko: 아이들이 청소차를 보면 신나서 손을 흔들어요.
examples.en: When children see the garbage truck, they wave excitedly.
The road is narrow, so even the garbage truck can't get in.

explain: '쓰레기차'라고도 말해요. 쓰레기를 모아 가는 차라서 '쓰레기를 싣다', '쓰레기를 수거하다'와 같이 나와요. 소방차, 구급차처럼 '-차' 이름의 특수한 차 중 하나예요.
explain_en: People also say '쓰레기차'. Since it collects trash, it appears with '쓰레기를 싣다' (load) and '쓰레기를 수거하다' (collect). It's one of the special vehicles with '-차' names, like '소방차' and '구급차'.

en: gym clothes; workout clothes; gym suit

examples.ko: 내일 체육 시간이 있어서 체육복을 입고 가야 해요.
examples.en: We have PE tomorrow, so I have to wear my gym clothes.
Please write your name on your gym clothes.

examples.ko: 이 체육복은 작아져서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: These gym clothes got too small, so I need to buy new ones.
My gym clothes got soaked with sweat, so I changed.
I put my gym clothes and sneakers in my bag.
The gym pants were too long, so I had them shortened.

explain: 학교에서 체육 시간에 입는 옷을 뜻할 때가 많아요. 일반적으로 운동할 때 입는 옷은 '운동복'이라고 해요. '체육복을 갈아입다', '체육복을 챙기다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It most often means the clothes worn in school PE class. Clothes for exercising in general are called '운동복'. Say '체육복을 갈아입다' (change into) or '체육복을 챙기다' (pack).

examples.en: Hotel check-out is until noon.
Pack all your things before check-out.
I asked whether I could check out late.
I returned the key card as I checked out.

examples.ko: 체크아웃 시간이 지나면 추가 요금이 붙어요.
examples.en: If you go past check-out time, an extra fee is added.

examples.ko: 공항에 가야 해서 일찍 체크아웃할 거예요.
examples.en: I have to go to the airport, so I'll check out early.

explain: 반대말은 '체크인'이에요. 호텔이나 숙소에서 방을 비우고 나가는 일이고, 일상에서는 '방을 빼다'라는 말도 써요. 시간은 '체크아웃 시간', 장소는 '프런트에서 체크아웃' 같이 말해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '체크인'. It means leaving the room at a hotel or lodging, and in everyday talk people also say '방을 빼다'. People say '체크아웃 시간' (check-out time) and '프런트에서 체크아웃' (check out at the front desk).

examples.ko: 한국어 초급반에서 한 달째 공부하고 있어요.
examples.en: I've been studying in a beginner Korean class for a month.
Lessons in the beginner class go slowly.
I signed up for a beginner swimming class.
Everyone in the beginner class works hard.
After taking the test, I was placed in the beginner class.
I finished the beginner class and moved up to intermediate.

explain: '초급반, 중급반, 고급반'이 세 단계로 짝이 돼요. 어학원이나 운동 강습에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 반을 옮길 때는 '올라가다', 배정할 때는 '배정되다'와 같이 나와요.
explain_en: '초급반, 중급반, 고급반' (beginner, intermediate, advanced) make a set of three levels. It's common at language schools and exercise classes. It goes with '올라가다' (move up) when changing classes and '배정되다' (be placed).

en: Chuseok day; the day of Chuseok

examples.ko: 추석날에는 온 가족이 모여서 송편을 빚어요.
examples.en: On Chuseok day, the whole family gathers to make songpyeon.

examples.ko: 추석날 아침에 일찍 일어나서 차례를 지내요.
examples.en: On the morning of Chuseok, we get up early and hold the ancestral rite.
It's a shame that Chuseok day overlaps with the weekend.

examples.ko: 추석날 길이 막힐까 봐 하루 전에 출발했어요.
examples.en: I left a day early, worried the roads would be jammed on Chuseok day.
This year on Chuseok day the moon was very bright.
There are people who work even on Chuseok day.

explain: '추석'은 명절 전체를 가리킬 때도 있고, '추석날'은 음력 8월 15일 그날을 콕 집어 말해요. 연휴 전체는 '추석 연휴'라고 해요. '설날'과 같이 날짜를 말하는 '-날' 표현이에요.
explain_en: '추석' can refer to the whole holiday, while '추석날' pinpoints the day itself, the 15th of the 8th lunar month. The whole break is called '추석 연휴'. Like '설날', it's a '-날' word naming a particular day.

examples.ko: 친할머니는 부산에 사시고 외할머니는 서울에 사세요.
examples.en: My paternal grandmother lives in Busan and my maternal grandmother in Seoul.
My grandmother on my father's side made kimchi herself for me.
Every vacation I go to my paternal grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 저는 친할머니를 많이 닮았다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: People tell me I look a lot like my paternal grandmother.
I was happy to get pocket money from my paternal grandmother.

examples.ko: 명절에는 친할머니 댁에 먼저 인사드리러 가요.
examples.en: On holidays we first go to greet my paternal grandmother.

explain: 아버지의 어머니를 말하고, 어머니의 어머니는 '외할머니'예요. 직접 부를 때는 그냥 '할머니'라고 하고 구분해서 이야기할 때만 '친할머니'라고 해요. 높임은 '친할머니께서', '친할머니께'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means your father's mother, while your mother's mother is '외할머니'. When addressing her directly you just say '할머니', and use '친할머니' only to distinguish when talking about her. For honorifics, use '친할머니께서' and '친할머니께'.

examples.en: My paternal grandfather takes a walk every morning.
My grandfather on my father's side told me old stories.
On New Year's Day I bowed to my paternal grandfather.
My paternal grandfather's house is in the countryside.
I take after my paternal grandfather, so I'm tall.
I put the photos of both grandfathers together.

explain: 아버지의 아버지를 말하고, 어머니의 아버지는 '외할아버지'예요. 직접 부를 때는 그냥 '할아버지'라고 해요. '친할아버지께서', '친할아버지께'처럼 높임 표현과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It means your father's father, while your mother's father is '외할아버지'. When addressing him directly you just say '할아버지'. It is used with honorific forms like '친할아버지께서' and '친할아버지께'.

examples.en: Shall we have curry rice for dinner today?
I put lots of potatoes and carrots in the curry rice.
Kids like curry rice.

examples.ko: 카레라이스는 만들기 쉬워서 자주 해 먹어요.
examples.en: Curry rice is easy to make, so we often cook it.
The curry rice was so spicy that I drank milk.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 카레라이스 한 접시에 팔천 원이에요.
examples.en: At this restaurant, a plate of curry rice is eight thousand won.

explain: 밥 위에 카레를 얹거나 부어 먹는 음식이고, 줄여서 '카레'라고도 많이 말해요. 그냥 '카레'는 소스를 가리킬 때도 있어요. '카레라이스를 만들다/먹다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It's rice served with curry on top, and people often shorten it to '카레'. Plain '카레' can also mean just the sauce. Say '카레라이스를 만들다' (make) or '먹다' (eat).

examples.ko: 커피콩을 갈아서 직접 커피를 내려 마셔요.
examples.en: I grind coffee beans and brew my own coffee.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 커피콩 향이 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: The smell of coffee beans in this shop is really nice.
The coffee tastes good only if the beans are fresh.
I got a bag of coffee beans as a gift.

examples.ko: 다른 나라에서 온 커피콩이라 향이 달라요.
examples.en: These beans come from another country, so the aroma is different.
It's best to store coffee beans sealed.

explain: 가게나 카페에서는 '원두'라는 말도 많이 써요. 볶기 전의 콩은 '생두'라고 해요. 콩 모양을 강조해서 말할 때 '커피콩'이라고 해요.
explain_en: At shops and cafés, people also use the word '원두'. Beans before roasting are called '생두'. '커피콩' is used when you emphasize the bean shape.
